name: Bacillus anthracis
notes: Chromosome is near-identical to the B. cereus group. Species call REQUIRES pXO1/pXO2 plasmid marker coverage, not chromosomal breadth alone.

name: Yersinia pestis
notes: >97% chromosomal ANI to Y. pseudotuberculosis. Discriminate on pPCP1/pMT1 plasmids and pseudogene content.

name: Francisella tularensis
notes: F. novicida is environmental and frequently miscalled as tularensis. Subspecies (tularensis vs holarctica) matters clinically; needs targeted loci.

name: Brucella melitensis
notes: Brucella spp. are >99% ANI to each other - species-level calls from metagenomes are usually NOT defensible. Report to genus unless marker loci resolve.

name: Brucella abortus
notes: See B. melitensis note. Also a vaccine strain (S19, RB51) source - check for vaccine-strain markers.

name: Brucella suis
notes: See B. melitensis note.

name: Burkholderia pseudomallei
notes: B. thailandensis is a common environmental soil organism and the main false-positive source.

name: Burkholderia mallei
notes: A clonal deletion derivative of B. pseudomallei - cannot be separated by breadth alone; requires absence-of-region logic.

name: Coxiella burnetii
notes: Obligate intracellular, low biomass. Expect few reads; weight marker genes over breadth.

name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
notes: MTBC members are ~99.9% ANI. Report as "M. tuberculosis complex" unless lineage SNPs resolve. BCG vaccine strain is M. bovis-derived.

name: Vibrio cholerae
notes: Non-toxigenic environmental V. cholerae is common. Toxigenicity requires ctxAB/tcpA coverage, not species call.

name: Salmonella enterica
notes: Serovar is the actionable unit, not species. Hand off to a dedicated serovar caller (sylph salmonella db is already on this box).

name: Listeria monocytogenes
notes: L. innocua is a frequent co-isolate; discriminate on the LIPI-1 island.

name: Legionella pneumophila
notes: Water-system contaminant of reagents is plausible - check controls.

name: Corynebacterium diphtheriae
notes: Toxigenicity is tox-gene dependent and phage-borne; species call is insufficient.

name: Neisseria meningitidis
notes: Commensal Neisseria in nasopharynx cross-map heavily. Capsule locus needed for serogroup.

name: Clostridium botulinum
notes: Polyphyletic species. Actionable signal is the BoNT gene cluster, which also occurs in C. butyricum/baratii.

name: Rickettsia prowazekii
notes: Obligate intracellular, low biomass.

name: Orientia tsutsugamushi
notes: Highly repetitive genome inflates depth CV; relax max_depth_cv.

name: Leptospira interrogans
notes: Saprophytic L. biflexa is environmental; pathogenic clade assignment matters.

name: Chlamydia psittaci
notes: Zoonotic; overlaps the animal pack.

name: Shigella dysenteriae
notes: Shigella is genomically E. coli. Species-level separation from metagenomes is unreliable; use ipaH plus lineage markers.

name: Escherichia coli
notes: Only pathotype is actionable (e.g. stx1/stx2/eae for STEC). Species presence is uninformative - gate reporting on virulence loci.

name: Bordetella pertussis
notes: IS481 is multi-copy and shared with B. holmesii - a classic false-positive route.

name: Streptococcus pyogenes
notes: Invasive disease is the notifiable event, not carriage.

name: Haemophilus influenzae
notes: H. haemolyticus is a commensal mimic; serotype b needs the cap locus.

name: Variola virus
notes: Orthopoxviruses are highly collinear. A variola call demands high breadth AND discriminating terminal-region content; vaccinia (vaccine/lab strain) is the dominant false-positive source. Escalate immediately on any credible hit.

name: Monkeypox virus
notes: Clade I vs II matters; requires breadth across variable regions.

name: Zaire ebolavirus
notes: Reston is non-pathogenic to humans - species resolution is essential, not optional.

name: Sudan ebolavirus
notes: See Zaire note.

name: Filoviridae
notes: GROUP-RANK ENTRY - capped at group_lead, never a species call. Exists so a divergent or novel filovirus with no reference of its own still surfaces: the classifier assigns its reads correctly to a species the watchlist does not hold, they roll up to this node, and every species-keyed row stays silent. Filoviridae has no commensal or environmental members, so a lead here is always worth following. Read lead.tsv, not sensitivity, to judge it.

name: Lassa mammarenavirus
notes: Segmented; require both L and S segments.

name: Junin mammarenavirus
notes: New World arenaviruses; vaccine strain Candid#1 exists.

name: Rift Valley fever phlebovirus
notes: Segmented (L/M/S); require multiple segments. Overlaps animal pack.

name: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever orthonairovirus
notes: Extremely high sequence diversity - low-identity thresholds needed or true positives are missed.

name: Hendra henipavirus
notes: Overlaps animal pack (equine).

name: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2
notes: Ubiquitous; laboratory and index-hopping contamination is the norm, not the exception. Control subtraction is mandatory.

name: Middle East respiratory syndrome-related coronavirus
notes: Overlaps animal pack (camelid).

name: Influenza A virus
notes: Segmented and reassorting. Subtype (HA/NA) is the actionable unit - a species call is not enough. Route to a segment-aware subtyper; flag H5/H7 explicitly.

name: Rabies lyssavirus
notes: Vaccine strains (ERA, SAD-B19, Pasteur) are common lab/wildlife-bait contaminants.

name: Enterovirus C
notes: Poliovirus surveillance context: Sabin vaccine strains and VDPV must be separated from wild-type. VP1 resolution required.

name: Measles morbillivirus
notes: Vaccine strain (Edmonston-derived) vs wild-type genotype separation is essential post-vaccination.

name: Yellow fever virus
notes: 17D vaccine strain is a frequent confounder.

name: Dengue virus
notes: Serotypes 1-4 are distinct enough to resolve; report serotype.

name: West Nile virus
notes: Overlaps animal pack (equine/avian).

name: Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus
notes: TC-83 vaccine strain exists. Overlaps animal pack.

name: Eastern equine encephalitis virus
notes: Overlaps animal pack.

name: Andes orthohantavirus
notes: Segmented; rodent-borne. Host-species context is diagnostic.

name: Hepatitis E virus
notes: Genotype 3/4 are zoonotic (swine) - overlaps animal pack.

name: Plasmodium falciparum
notes: 23 Mb AT-rich genome; breadth accumulates slowly - low min_breadth is correct here, not a mistake. Species mix is common in endemic settings.

name: Plasmodium vivax
notes: P. knowlesi is morphologically confused with vivax/malariae - sequence resolution is the advantage here.

name: Plasmodium knowlesi
notes: Zoonotic (macaque).

name: Trypanosoma brucei
notes: Subspecies gambiense/rhodesiense are the human-infective forms; b. brucei is not. Resolution requires SRA/TgsGP loci.

name: Trypanosoma cruzi
notes: T. rangeli is non-pathogenic and cross-maps.

name: Leishmania donovani
notes: L. donovani/infantum complex is barely separable; report to complex.

name: Entamoeba histolytica
notes: E. dispar is non-pathogenic, morphologically identical, and the single most important false positive in this genus.

name: Toxoplasma gondii
notes: H. hammondi is ~99% identical and non-pathogenic to humans.

name: Cryptosporidium parvum
notes: parvum (zoonotic) vs hominis (anthroponotic) distinction drives the outbreak investigation.

name: Cryptosporidium hominis
notes: See C. parvum note.

name: Giardia intestinalis
notes: Assemblages A/B are human-infective; C-H are animal. Assemblage matters.

name: Naegleria fowleri
notes: Free-living; water-system reagent contamination is plausible.

name: Balamuthia mandrillaris
notes: Rare, often only detected by sequencing - low read counts are expected and still meaningful.

name: Acanthamoeba castellanii
notes: Environmental; interpret with care.

name: Echinococcus granulosus
notes: Overlaps animal pack (canid/livestock).

name: Echinococcus multilocularis
notes: Overlaps animal pack.

name: Taenia solium
notes: Neurocysticercosis risk is solium-specific; saginata is not.

name: Schistosoma mansoni
notes: Hybridisation with animal schistosomes is documented - expect chimeric signal.

name: Trichinella spiralis
notes: Overlaps animal pack (swine/game).

name: Coccidioides immitis
notes: immitis/posadasii are geographically distinct but genomically close; report to genus if unresolved.

name: Coccidioides posadasii
notes: See C. immitis note.

name: Histoplasma capsulatum
notes: Now split into multiple cryptic species; taxonomy is unstable - re-resolve often.

name: Blastomyces dermatitidis
notes: B. gilchristii was split out of dermatitidis; both are pathogenic.

name: Talaromyces marneffei
notes: Environmental Penicillium is ubiquitous in reagents; discriminate carefully.

name: Cryptococcus gattii
notes: gattii affects immunocompetent hosts - the species call changes clinical interpretation. Endemic in BC/PNW.

name: Cryptococcus neoformans
notes: See C. gattii note.

name: Candida auris
notes: Multidrug-resistant, outbreak-prone in healthcare. C. haemulonii complex is the misidentification route. Clade assignment is epidemiologically useful.

name: Aspergillus fumigatus
notes: Ubiquitous airborne contaminant - a positive means little without clinical context. Azole-resistance cyp51A alleles are the actionable signal.

name: Pneumocystis jirovecii
notes: Cannot be cultured; sequencing is a primary detection route. Colonisation vs disease is not resolvable by sequence.

name: Rhizopus arrhizus
notes: Mucorales; environmental and a common reagent contaminant.

name: Fusarium solani
notes: Species complex; overlaps plant pack. Outbreak source has included contaminated medical products.
